At 1.3 million cells the GPU pipeline took 435 s against 52,056 s on CPU (119.6-fold; 105.5-fold in a run that differed only in data loading). Wilcoxon differential expression accounted for 93.5% of the CPU time; without it the speedup was 7.9-9.2-fold. Pseudo-bulk differential expression finished 44 times sooner than the cell-level t-test at 3.4 million cells. For spatial data we rebuilt the CPU reference with one fresh process per repeat and the same cell groups for CPU and GPU. Against this DGX CPU reference, an RTX 4090 accelerated end-to-end analysis 1.4-fold on Visium v1, 6.9-fold on Visium HD 8 um (without co-occurrence) and 10.4-fold on Visium HD 2 um.
